h: Fort Douglas, Mines and a Famous Chapel
p: Dalkeith Country Park has a trick up its sleeve for families with little ones: Fort Douglas, a big timber adventure play area with towers, tunnels and slides. It's a brilliant way to keep younger children busy while older siblings are up on the high ropes, and everyone can swap notes afterwards over a hot drink at the Restoration Yard, the park's shop and café hub in the old stable buildings.

For the treetop session, budget a couple of hours, plus a little time to park and find the meeting point. Scottish weather can do four seasons before lunch, so a thin waterproof and a warm layer you can stuff in a pocket are worth their weight in gold.

Midlothian has some cracking follow-ups nearby. The National Mining Museum Scotland at Newtongrange tells the story of the area's coal-mining past in a real former colliery. Rosslyn Chapel at Roslin, famous for its astonishing stone carvings, is a short drive away and fascinating whether or not you've read The Da Vinci Code.

If you've got the energy for more action, Midlothian Snowsports Centre at Hillend, on the edge of the Pentland Hills, offers dry-slope skiing and great views over Edinburgh. And of course, the city itself is close enough to finish your day with a wander up the Royal Mile.
